subject: general
question: Who among the following scholar translated Patanjali’s work on grammar into Arabic?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Al-Biruni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Al-Biruni **lived in the eastern Islamic world during an era of unprecedented political instability.
 
• He was a servant to more than six princes. Al-Biruni spent years acquiring Sanskrit and studying religious and philosophical writings in the presence of Brahmana priests and academics.
 
• Because Al-Biruni was fluent in numerous languages, he was able to compare and translate writings. He translated various Sanskrit books into Arabic, notably Patanjali's grammar work.
 
• Patanjali wrote '**Mahabhasya**; an ancient treatise on Sanskrit grammar and linguistics, based on the **Astadhyayi **of Panini. 
 
• He translated the works of Euclid (a Greek mathematician) into Sanskrit for his Brahmana companions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ibn Hajar al-Haytami** was a muhaddith and Islamic theologian from Egypt.
 
• **Ibn al-Hajj **was a Moroccan theologian and Maliki fiqh scholar. He was born in Fes and lived till 1336 in Egypt.
 
• **Ibn Hubal's **medical compendium, Kitab al-Mukhtarat fi al-Tibb, or "The Book of Selections in Medicine," was his most famous work.
